title: Butler duty template
description: Schema for recipe.json, the manifest at the root of a duty-template bundle (recipe.json, duty.py, README.md). This shape is fixed by the container's template installer — a field outside it is refused, never merged in.

id.description: Must equal the `name` this template is listed under in templates.json — that is the ref a duty is created with (<id>@<version>).

version.description: A plain, monotonic integer — not semver. A ref is `<id>@<version>`.

description.description: Composed into a 280-char field with a settings clause appended — a longer one is silently dropped by the caller, so the validator refuses it here instead.

supersedes.description: Older refs this version replaces, e.g. ["dca@1"]. Flattened into the published index's top-level `aliases`.

keys.description: The stable idempotency-key format(s) this template's duty.py uses, documentation only — e.g. "buy:<duty>:slot:<slot>".

params.description: A JSON-Schema OBJECT describing the settings a duty created from this template takes. Only the subset of JSON-Schema the container's params checker supports may appear anywhere in this tree (see recipe-params-subset.schema.json for the exact keyword allowlist, enforced recursively by scripts/validate.py's check_params_schema), plus one root-only conditional-required escape hatch, `allOf` (see below).

allOf.description: Root-only conditional-required subset the container's params checker enforces (conditionalClauses in recipe-params.mjs) and scripts/validate.py's check_params_conditionals validates: [{if: {properties: {<name>: {const: ...} | {enum: [...]}}}, then: {required: [...]}}, ...]. A condition holds only when the named property is present; `then` contributes `required` alone. Refused anywhere below the root.
